sum.dish: Nearly every review orders the marinated beef galbi + naengmyeon combo to finish.
sum.vibe: Loud, smoky, classic K-BBQ energy — staff grill the meat for you.
sum.wait: ~30 min at dinner peak (7–8pm). Walk-ins OK before 6pm.
sum.tip: Reviewers say solo staff speak basic English and there's a photo menu.

sum.dish: Salt bread and hand-drip single origin are the two things everyone mentions.
sum.vibe: Renovated red-brick factory, industrial-cool — the 'Seongsu look'.
sum.wait: Seats turn over fast; weekends busy 2–5pm but queue moves quickly.
sum.tip: Order at the counter; card only, no cash — foreign cards fine.

sum.dish: Hand-cut knife noodles in anchovy broth; kimchi is self-serve and praised.
sum.vibe: No-frills local lunch spot — plastic stools, fast service, mostly regulars.
sum.tip: Korean-only menu, but only 4 items — reviewers say pointing works fine.

sum.dish: 12-course lunch omakase is the value pick (~₩60,000).
sum.vibe: 8-seat counter facing Seoul Forest; quiet, intimate, chef chats in English.
sum.tip: Phone booking only. Ask your hotel concierge to call, or use our call service (coming soon).

sum.dish: Seafood pancake + house makgeolli; locals call it the best jeon in Seongsu.
sum.vibe: Retro alley pub, packed after 7pm, very local — almost no tourists.
sum.wait: 45–60 min Fri/Sat nights. No waitlist app — you queue in person.
sum.tip: CASH ONLY for foreign cards (Korean cards OK). ATM is 2 min away.

sum.dish: 1++ hanwoo tasting set for two; doenjang stew finish is repeatedly praised.
sum.vibe: Modern, quieter than most BBQ spots — good for conversation.
sum.wait: Bookable, so near-zero if reserved. Walk-in ~20 min.
sum.tip: Has private rooms for 6–10 — reviewers recommend for family dinners.

sum.dish: Ricotta pancakes and the bulgogi benedict (K-fusion) split reviewers evenly.
sum.vibe: Bright plant-filled space; stroller-friendly, lots of families on weekends.
sum.wait: Weekend 11am–1pm queue ~25 min; weekdays walk right in.
sum.tip: Full English menu + English-speaking staff — easiest brunch in the area.

sum.dish: Whole chicken hotpot for sharing — add the hand-cut noodles at the end.
sum.vibe: Steamy, communal, big round tables — made for groups of 4–8.
sum.wait: ~20 min at dinner; big tables free up slowly.
sum.tip: Menu is Korean-only but there are only 3 options; staff gesture the steps.

sum.dish: Temple-style mushroom bowl; vegan kimchi jjigae surprises meat-eaters.
sum.vibe: Calm, minimalist; popular with international long-stay visitors.
sum.tip: One of very few fully-vegan Korean places east of the river — book ahead Sundays.

sum.dish: ₩12,000 mackerel set with 8 banchan — reviewers call it the best-value lunch nearby.
sum.vibe: Homey, ajumma-run; feels like a Korean grandmother's kitchen.
sum.tip: Point at the fish display to order — no shared language needed, and it works.

sum.dish: Beef gopchang mixed grill; fried rice finish is described as mandatory.
sum.vibe: Open till 2am — where locals go after round one. Loud and fun.
sum.wait: Peak 9–11pm, ~40 min. After midnight you walk in.
sum.tip: Adventurous eaters only — reviews warn first-timers to start with the mixed set.

sum.dish: Perilla-oil pasta (K-Italian) is the signature everyone photographs.
sum.vibe: Dim, 12-seat wine bar; couples only by design — no groups.
sum.tip: Corkage-free Mondays gets mentioned in half the recent reviews.
